crisis.label: High
crisis.detail: Aug 5: Treasury Secretary Bessent said the US and Iran could reach a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz with 'freedom of movement' for commercial ships 'today or tomorrow' (CNBC, Aug 4), and Qatar said a proposed de-escalation resolution is being circulated between the parties (Trading Economics, Aug 4-5). Rubio confirmed progress but said no final deal has been reached (ABC/AP, Aug 4). Security risk persists: UKMTO reported a second vessel struck by an unknown projectile 20nm northeast of Khasab at 22:00 UTC Aug 3, the same location as the prior day's tanker explosion report (Windward MIOC, Aug 4). Markets sold off hard on the deal signal Tuesday - Brent -5.8% to $78.88, WTI -6.3% to $75.26, TTF -5% to ~55 EUR/MWh (Trading Economics) - then steadied Wednesday (Brent $79.18, -0.2%). Crisis level cut to 4 (High); tail cut to 30%.

todaysEvents.summary: US says Hormuz deal could come within days
todaysEvents.delta: Down: Treasury Secretary Bessent told CNBC the US and Iran could reach a deal to open the Strait with 'freedom of movement' for commercial ships 'today or tomorrow', expecting prices to fall further as trapped vessels exit. Source: CNBC, Aug 4.

Down: Qatar said a proposed de-escalation resolution is being circulated between the parties and an interim proposal has been prepared; Rubio confirmed progress but cautioned no final deal to reopen the strait has been reached. Source: Trading Economics; ABC/AP, Aug 4-5.

todaysEvents.summary: Second vessel struck off Khasab in 24 hours
todaysEvents.delta: Up: UKMTO reported a cargo vessel struck by an unknown projectile 20nm NE of Khasab at 22:00 UTC Aug 3 - the same location as the prior day's tanker explosion report - with identity and damage unreleased. Source: Windward MIOC, Aug 4.

scenarios.label: Base
scenarios.description: Bessent's 'today or tomorrow' window and Qatar's de-escalation resolution convert into a signed Oman-mediated reopening within days, with traffic normalising on a phased basis under Iranian/Omani routing oversight (NYT/AP, Aug 3-4). Brent drifts toward $70-80 as trapped Gulf vessels exit and the LNG risk premium unwinds.

scenarios.label: Stress
scenarios.description: Negotiations continue but stop short of a signed deal: Iran keeps insisting on controlling maritime traffic, sporadic attacks persist (a second vessel struck off Khasab within 24 hours, UKMTO via Windward, Aug 3), and Hormuz traffic recovers only gradually (about 15/day vs the roughly 88/day pre-war norm). Brent holds $75-90 and JKM stays elevated on Qatar force majeure through mid-September.

scenarios.label: Tail
scenarios.description: The talks collapse as the Jul 26-30 pause did: Trump's 'last chance' warning expires, US strikes resume, and Iran retaliates against shipping and Gulf states. Brent returns to $105-135+/bbl and JKM above $30/MMBtu as the strait closes again.

traceInputs.headline: Windward MIOC data (Aug 4) shows 15 Hormuz crossings in the 21:00-UTC Aug 2-3 window (10 outbound, 5 inbound; 4 dark-AIS) - the first outbound LPG cargo in 11 days - while Kpler (Aug 3) put weekly crossings at about 15/day (+8% w/w) with 3 LNG tanker transits, the first sustained LNG-specific movement since the carried July 18 zero-transit observation. Qatar force majeure remains confirmed through mid-September, with a further extension to mid-October reportedly in preparation but not yet formally confirmed. Bessent said a US-Iran deal to reopen the Strait could come 'today or tomorrow' (CNBC, Aug 4) and Qatar is circulating a de-escalation resolution, but no final agreement is signed and current route-cost data remains unavailable.

priceNarratives.Brent: Pre-shock ~$65 -> $126 wartime high intraday (Day 59, Apr 30, CNBC/CNN) -> $98.57 (Jun 3 D93 peak) -> $90.12 (Aug 1, Yahoo Finance BZ=F) as tanker incidents and Kuwait attacks kept risk elevated -> $83.61 (Aug 3, -4.9%, Investing.com) as Trump canceled planned strikes -> $84.28 (Aug 4 intraday, +0.8%, Trading Economics) as Iran denied a full reopening deal -> $78.88 (Aug 4 close, -5.8%, Trading Economics) as Bessent said a US-Iran deal to open Hormuz could come 'today or tomorrow' and Qatar began circulating a de-escalation resolution -> $79.18 (Aug 5, -0.2%, Trading Economics) as the market weighed the prospective reopening against Iran's insistence on controlling traffic. Yahoo's BZ=F/CL=F/TTF=F/EURUSD=X feeds again carried stale chartPreviousClose references on Aug 5 (spuriously implying an 11% plunge), so Trading Economics remains the confirmed source. Working range $70-85 base (signed deal); $75-90 stress (stalled talks); $105-135+ tail (collapse).
priceNarratives.JKM LNG: Baseline $9.5 -> $23.40/MMBtu (Day 20, Reuters/Platts) -> $19.93/MMBtu (Jul 16, Trading Economics) -> $22.00/MMBtu (Jul 24, Reuters Sept-delivery assessment) as sustained Hormuz disruption tightened Asian LNG balances; carried at $22.00 pending a newer weekly assessment. Contextual CFD reference $21.18/MMBtu (Trading Economics, Aug 4, -0.38%). Qatar force majeure remains confirmed to mid-September (Reuters, Jul 23), with a further extension to mid-October reportedly in preparation (Bloomberg, Jul 22, unconfirmed).
priceNarratives.TTF Gas: Pre-shock ~$34/MWh -> 63.58/MWh (Jul 24, +2.71% vs Jul 23, MacroMicro) -> 59.07/MWh (Jul 31, +1.4%, Yahoo Finance TTF=F) as tanker incidents kept the supply-risk premium elevated -> 56.06 EUR/MWh (Aug 3, -5.1%, Trading Economics) as Trump's strike stand-down eased the risk premium -> 58.12 EUR/MWh (Aug 4 intraday, +3.7%, Trading Economics) -> about 55.0 EUR/MWh (Aug 4 close, -5%, Trading Economics) as Bessent's deal signal and Qatar's de-escalation resolution capped the risk premium -> 55.06 EUR/MWh (Aug 5, +0.1%, Trading Economics). The marker remains elevated versus the pre-crisis baseline on persistent Qatar LNG disruption and 57%-full EU storage.

Tail cut to 30% while no final agreement is signed and a second vessel was struck off Khasab within 24 hours.
